quest.title: Where the Dandelions Find Rest
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Momoyo! Momoyo! Where are yooou?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, this place has been trashed by the Fatui. Momoyo's stuff... and the materials... They're all gone!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like this safehouse isn't safe anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But what's happened to Momoyo? Was she... captured by the Fatui!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, wait a moment. There's been this weird smell ever since we entered the safehouse. There's something in the air here...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's powder on the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Powder? Is that the elemental powder we used the last time? C'mon, {NICKNAME}, use your Elemental Sight, quick! This has to be a message that Momoyo left for us in her time of need!

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: What? Was there anything else?

response.speaker: Momoyo
response.text: It's fine, it won't impede my mobility. I might even be able to infiltrate a pirate crew at some point in the future. That would be interesting for sure.

choices.text: What do you plan to do after this?

response.speaker: Momoyo
response.text: First, we need to wipe out those Fatui who are planning to plant poison on Watatsumi Island. However, their Teacher appears to have left Inazuma. Hmph. If he ever dares to return, I'll make sure he never leaves again.

response.speaker: Momoyo
response.text: Someone is helping me pass the intel to the Shuumatsuban. Don't you worry.

response.speaker: Momoyo
response.text: Some shortie named Sayu. She told me that she knows you two. She should be passing our news on to the Shuumatsuban right about now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You sure everything will be okay?

response.speaker: Momoyo
response.text: Yes, yes. I know she doesn't look very reliable. But she's still a Shuumatsuban ninja. She won't act carelessly when important matters are at stake.

response.speaker: Momoyo
response.text: She also said that she would've tried harder if she knew that you were going to use that code sheet.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Tried harder to remember all the codes?

response.speaker: Momoyo
response.text: "Tried harder not to drool all over the sheet."

response.speaker: Momoyo
response.text: Bye. Quickly now, go to Ritou.

response.speaker: Momoyo
response.text: ...Momoka, it was you who took me in and allowed me to join the Shuumatsuban back when I was an orphan. Have I... finally made you proud?

talks.objective: Enter the basement of the abandoned building.
Follow the elemental trail to search for Momoyo

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: *cough* I've said this before. I've got nothing to say to you pieces of garbage. If you're going to finish me, do it soon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Momoyo!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're here to save you.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: #Paimon and {NICKNAME}? Hah. To think that you'd find this place, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, quit talking tough. Since you left the elemental powder behind, you must've believed that we come to rescue you!

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Hmph. Then what would you like me to do? Praise your skills?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehehe. That can wait till later. Let's get you out of here first. Come on, let's go get that door!

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: The door's locked. The key should be with their superior.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: They seem to have been notified of something halfway through the interrogation, since they left in a hurry.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: They should be plotting in secret in the room on the highest floor.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: It's likely that they have locked the door from the other side while this is happening. You'll need special magatama to unlock it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got it.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Alright. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: This is... a Fortune Slip from the Grand Narukami Shrine?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! We got this the day we used the fake Bamboo Slip to tail you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Bamboo Slip may have been fake, sure, but it was the key to us being able to truly understand you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You were the one who told us that we were good people, and that the fortune would definitely be accurate as a result.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're a good person too, Lyudochka. So we're sure that good fortune will go with you as well!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We hope that it'll help you remember the times you spent in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: May you do as the Fortune Slip says: "Fly, drift, across the seas, to lands far away..."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "But one day, you will no longer drift."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "One day, you will become what you hope to be."

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: "One day, you will become what you hope to be..."

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: What I... Hope to be...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ms. Lyudochka. You say that your life has no direction, but that's not true. You're just being tied down by your past.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In fact, you already knew what sort of person you'd like to become!

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: I... already knew?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The shrine maiden uniform you're wearing—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is your answer!

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: I... *sobs*

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: *sobs* I—It's true. You're right! I always... I always wanted to become a real shrine maiden!

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: Every day, whenever people would get their Bamboo Slips from the Fortune Slip Box, whenever they would earnestly share their troubles with me, I would feel guilty about being a fraud.

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: I really wished that I could bring them joy!

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: #*sobs* {NICKNAME}, Paimon... Can my wish really come true?

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: Can I really stay? Can I really become that person?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Momoyo says that you can continue using the name "Gendou Ringo" — if you're willing to, of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You'll never have to be tied down by the name Lyudochka ever again!

response.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
response.text: *sniff* Thank you... Thank you all...

response.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
response.text: I will take up this name. I will become the real "Gendou Ringo."

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Lyudochka takes a moment to calm down.\nAfterward, you return the Mora she sent back to her.

response.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
response.text: *sigh* Sorry for the trouble, you two. It must have been hard to convince me to stay.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, all's well that ends well, right? Are you feeling better now?

response.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
response.text: I am. I'm sure of what I feel now. I want to stay here in Inazuma, at the Grand Narukami Shrine.

response.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
response.text: Since I've taken the Mora back, please, take this Fortune Slip. May my blessing go with you.

response.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
response.text: I'll return to the shrine now. Hopefully, I can thank Ms. Momoyo in person. I must also thank Lady Yae for taking me in...

response.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
response.text: #See you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. Let's meet again at the Grand Narukami Shrine.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: See you, Lyudochka.

response.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
response.text: Hehe. Next time we meet, just call me "Gendou Ringo."

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you're back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Momoyo, are you okay... *gasp* You're hurt all over!

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: #Quit your yelling. It's not that bad... Would you mind supporting me, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, you can't even walk by yourself. You're not okay at all! Wait a moment. Why aren't you looking at us? What happened to your eyes?

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Heh. When I was going for the elemental powder box, some Fatui shot the box and broke it. Some of the stuff got into my eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't you say the elemental powder was poisonous?

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: You're way too noisy. I doubt I'm going to lose both eyes. It's just that this place is too dark for me to see anything. Let's get outside first.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Phew. That was one musty cell. Guess I can finally breathe easy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Momoyo! What happened to your eyes!?

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Oh, relax. This one's fine now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But your other eye...

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Bah. What's with those sad faces?

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Be glad! We fooled them all and even exposed their base, all for the cost of only one eye. This is a worthy trade!

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Hehehe, that Teacher was completely taken in by my handiwork. That Fatui girl you're trying to save will never have to live in fear again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... You mean you didn't flee from the safehouse because you wanted them to believe that Lyudochka was dead?

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: We had an agreement. And anyway, it would be a waste of all our previous effort if we were to be exposed at this juncture.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: In any case, I expected that you would come to rescue me.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Well, this capture of mine was quite sudden, and we have an upcoming mission in Watatsumi Island, so there's no time for a written report.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: I'll just have to go to the Grand Narukami Shrine and get someone to pass a message to the Shuumatsuban.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: As for you, go tell Lyudochka that she's safe now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we'll do just that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ms. Lyudochka, we're back! We've done it! You're safe now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ms. Lyudochka?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She's not in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's weird. Where did she go? Let's ask the Yae Publishing House employees. They might know a thing or two.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Is there anything I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there. We'd like to ask after someone. Do you know where the lady who's been doing proofreading these few days has gone? We're friends of hers.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: #Oh, you must be {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Ms. Touyama said that you'd come looking for her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Ms. Touyama?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That should be Lyudochka's pseudonym.)

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: She told me yesterday that she won't be able to continue working here due to a family emergency.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: What a shame! A dexterous and diligent proofreader is hard to find. I was actually going to ask her to go full time with us, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Right. Here's something that she wanted to pass to you before she left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She left us a letter!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ms. Lyudochka says... she's leaving. And she's left a sum of Mora for us and Momoyo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that really okay, though? Let's... Let's go ask Momoyo.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Huh, you're back. How did it go? I suppose that Fatui girl can be at ease now, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Momoyo about the letter and Mora Lyudochka left behind.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: What? She's leaving?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like it...

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Pfft. Seriously? "Ms. Momoyo lost an eye on my account"? Nonsense. It's not like she blinded me personally or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: The injury was an occupational hazard, you know? If anyone should be compensating me, it should be the Shuumatsuban.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, I don't need her Mora. You can do whatever you want with it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you say that, but honestly, even Paimon isn't sure if we should...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, struggling about Mora? Say it isn't so!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Paimon isn't that Mora-faced!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But where's she going to go after leaving Inazuma? Can she really find a new life and happiness?

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Huh, that reminds me. I don't think I can go back to doing shrine maiden work looking like this.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: The Lady Guuji told me earlier that she thought our impostor was pretty suited for the job.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Heh. I'd hate to think about what she would do to you if she finds out that you've chased her shrine maiden candidate away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Wait a moment, why is that our fault?

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Are you saying it isn't? You didn't stop her, and now she's about to flee Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Paimon's got it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Momoyo!

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: She'll probably be looking for a way to get out through Ritou. Best to look for her there.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: When you bring her back, tell her she can keep using the name "Gendou Ringo" — if she's willing to take it up, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: I gave it to myself on a whim, but turns out that it fits her decently well, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Hurry up and get going. I'm leaving her to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Alright, {NICKNAME}, to Ritou's harbor it is! We've gotta get Ms. Lyudochka back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ms. Lyudochka! We finally found you!

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... Why are you two here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're here to ask you to turn back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Momoyo doesn't need your Mora, and neither do we! Just use it to make a new life for yourself here in Inazuma!

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: What... What are you saying...

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: I was a Fatui, you know? We threatened Inazuma's safety! And I caused you all so much trouble. I don't deserve to stay here, not after all that.

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: And even if you'd like me to stay... Does anyone else?

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: Is there really anyone who needs me here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's not how it is at all! There are other people who'd like you to stay! Like... Like...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Momoyo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! We were only able to find you because of her instructions!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Momoyo said that it wasn't your fault that she lost an eye. It's an occupational hazard and the Shuumatsuban should be paying the cost instead!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The "occupational hazard" bit seems unnecessary...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? But why? That's what Momoyo said, and it's pretty convincing!

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: But... But...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, do you need more evidence that people would like to have you back? Don't worry, there are others, like...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ms. Aratani.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly, exactly! Ms. Aratani said that you're "dexterous and diligent." She even said that she'd like you to become a full-time employee at Yae Publishing House!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although Paimon personally thinks that you shouldn't take up a job at Yae Publishing House — unless you want some super deep eyebags!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you really have to say that, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why not! Ms. Lyudochka's gonna have to pick her occupation carefully if she stays. Our suggestions are super important!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks that being a shrine maiden would be best for you.

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: But that's not a place where someone like me can just go to whenever she wants...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No need to worry about that! You've got a super big shot vouching for you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Guuji Yae.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She knew that you were an impostor the whole time, but she also thinks that you'd be suited to working at the shrine!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Also, Momoyo can't go back to work there, so if Guuji Yae finds out that you're not coming back either... {NICKNAME} and Paimon are doomed for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That sounds like a threat...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No it's not! Paimon's just employing both emotion and reason, that's all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And aren't you even the least bit worried that Miko is really gonna put us through the wringer?

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: Heh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You finally smiled! Does that mean you're not leaving anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: #Paimon, {NICKNAME}, thank you both so much. And the people who accepted me... They have my thanks as well.

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: But... I've been trained in spycraft since I was young. Before coming to Inazuma, I had never once experienced an ordinary life.

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: As a "Snezhevna," I still do not know where I truly belong.

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: And I do not know if someone as steeped in darkness as myself has the right to return to walk in the light...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ms. Lyudochka...

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: So perhaps leaving Inazuma and exploring the various regions of Teyvat might actually be good for me, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: At the very least, I'd have the chance to think about the sort of person I'd really hope to become.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you love Inazuma so much! Won't you have regrets if you just leave like this?

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: Yes, I will miss this place... But there's no other option, is there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How could this be? Ms. Lyudochka was starting to waver back there, but she just doesn't wanna admit it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like convincing her to stay is gonna be hard no matter what we say.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We could still take the opposite approach.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's drop her guard first.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then make her face her own heart's desire head-on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh. That's true. It's not that she doesn't have dreams, but she doesn't dare to face herself because she's worried that she doesn't deserve to be happy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, oh! Paimon knows! We've got something with us that can help!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll convince her for sure this time!

dialogues.speaker: Momoyo
dialogues.text: Well? Found the key yet?

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: I know you have good intentions... But I've already decided to do this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You misunderstand us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, we're not going to convince you anymore. But since you're leaving Inazuma, we thought that we should at least give you something before we part ways — y'know, for good fortune!

dialogues.speaker: Lyudochka Snezhevna
dialogues.text: Huh? What is it, then?
